title: Perplexity to open source tool used to contain AI agents
key_facts: Perplexity AI released SPACE, a sandbox that isolates AI agents, as open source on 15 Oct 2026.
SPACE was built to protect Perplexity's own Computer agents; each agent runs in a small virtual machine with its own operating system.
Network access and credentials are managed outside the sandbox, which is treated as untrusted; the system takes snapshots and checkpoints so work can be rolled back.
CoreWeave, Akamai and Crusoe are already deploying it, according to the article.
Perplexity engineer Zibi Braniecki told Semafor the team tested nine frontier models in 118 attempts to break out; none escaped, though some got around network restrictions, which were then fixed.
Perplexity says agents escaped from several other proprietary sandboxes in the same tests.
Nvidia's OpenShell, released last month, is another open-source agent sandbox.
quote_evidence: The company has developed an AI sandbox specifically for isolating AI agents called SPACE, and it's being made open source from today.
In 118 attempts, none of them succeeded, though some did manage to find their way around the network restrictions.
Braniecki said the open-source nature of SPACE is key to securing AI agents.
why_it_matters_hint: Agents escaping sandboxes has caused real incidents, so a shared open-source containment tool lets other developers use the same protection; the escape test results are Perplexity's own.
